split.method: Group-level random split: all paraphrases of a concept share a group and stay on the same side.

configuration.fusion: Reciprocal rank fusion (c=60) of BM25 and semantic top-15

query_forms.normalized: abbreviation expansion + category label from the Nivaaran lexicon

configuration.metadata_filter: Each query searches only clauses active in its policy version (superseded clauses removed).
configuration.verification: Production path: union of BM25 and semantic top-8 candidates -> clause-term verification -> decision rules.

metric_definitions.hit@k: Share of queries with at least one relevant clause in the top k.
metric_definitions.precision@3: Mean of |relevant ∩ top-3| / 3 (bounded above when a query has fewer than 3 relevant clauses).
metric_definitions.mrr: Mean reciprocal rank of the first relevant clause (0 if none in the top 10).
metric_definitions.ndcg@5: Graded nDCG with gains 2^rel - 1 (rel 2 = decisive, 1 = related).
metric_definitions.accuracy: Share of labeled bill items whose predicted evidence label equals the gold label.

verification.unsupported_answer_rate_definition: Share of items whose correct answer is non-definitive (conditional, conflict or insufficient evidence) for which the system nevertheless returned covered/excluded.

limitations: Small synthetic dataset (one demo policy, one endorsement); results do not generalise to real policy wordings.

Queries, labels and the normalisation lexicon were written by the same team, so the 'normalized' query form may be optimistic even on the held-out split; the 'raw' rows show performance without the lexicon.

The dev split was used for inspection while building the pipeline; no parameters were tuned on the eval split. One dev-split error was fixed during development: 'Blood bank processing charges' was wrongly verified as covered under 2.5 because the bare word 'blood' mapped to the laboratory category; the keyword was narrowed.
Verification metrics depend on deterministic, pattern-based clause interpretation tuned to clearly drafted wordings.
